rules: Every fact here is from a capture, as the researcher wrote it; the curator added none, checked none and rewrote no source (checking is the fact-checker's job). Public material only; no contact details; people named only in their public, professional role.

captures.what_is_new: The 2026 dates (9 to 12 November) and venue (MEO Arena and FIL, Parque das Nações); the venue map will be in the app.
captures.is_story: service, not a story on its own

captures.what_is_new: Where and when to collect lanyards and wristbands: Lisbon airport Terminal 1 or Pavilhão de Portugal, from Saturday 7 November; bring the ticket in the app and photo ID; times may change.
Getting there: Oriente metro (red line) about 300 metres from the MEO Arena; Carris shuttle and lines; a discounted 1, 3 or 5 day transport pass.
Inside the venue: small bags, two bag drops, cashless stands, free wifi in the MEO Arena, own food and reusable cup allowed, lost and found in Pavilion 5.
The app holds the ticket as a QR code needed to register, builds a schedule, finds people and companies, books meetings; no built-in chat.
Three public passes and their prices as read (General 1,595, VIP 1,950, Chairperson 24,950 euros).
captures.is_story: no: reference only, five days out; kept as a fact for the summit's logistics page

captures.what_is_new: 17 content tracks over four days, including AI Summit, Policy Summit, Cybersecurity Summit, Energy Summit, Health Summit, MoneyConf, Venture Summit, Developer Summit.
The schedule is live and grows weekly; a meetup for first-time attendees on Tuesday 10 November at 11am.
captures.is_story: yes, as part of G1 and G2

captures.what_is_new: First State of the Industry survey (1,455 respondents, 22 October 2026): 55% say AI strengthens their critical thinking, 60% say it has increased their workload; 70,000+ attendees from 100+ countries and 10,000 startups expected.
16 digital creators in the Creator Programme (announced 21 October 2026) will document Lisbon live from the floor.
captures.is_story: small: a line in G2 or the agenda; no creator is named in the capture

captures.what_is_new: In 2025 over 22,000 startups applied to the startup programme and about 2,700 were accepted, in ALPHA, BETA and GROWTH.
captures.is_story: yes, as context for G3 and G4

names: HaDEA (European Health and Digital Executive Agency)
captures.what_is_new: HaDEA at stand E418, Pavilion 4, all week; a session on EU funding for technological sovereignty on 11 November at 15.30 with four EU-funded projects.

Road 2 Web Summit, 11th edition: up to 125 Portuguese startups, a bootcamp in Porto and Lisbon, 50% off ALPHA or BETA, space on the Portugal stand; in 2025, 115 startups raised 40 million euros; Galp sponsors two prizes (15,000 and 5,000 euros).

captures.what_is_new: Granter, PITCH winner in November 2025, raised 1.6 million euros to expand into Spain, Germany and Italy (reported 3 November 2026).
Seamoretech, a University of Porto spin-off recovering freshwater and minerals from desalination brine, raised 1.1 million euros in a first seed closing; commercial launch in Spain planned for 2027.
Algarve Evolution (Faro) aims to support 500 companies, help create 150 startups and reach 50,000 people in the Algarve by 2032, beyond tourism.

captures.what_is_new: Unicorn Factory Lisboa's 2026 Entrepreneurship Awards (27 October, its fourth anniversary): BloodFlow (most promising), knok (most impactful), RTBeamTech (youth).
Intuitivo, a past PITCH winner, raised 1.35 million euros to expand into Brazil; its platform serves 500+ schools and 75,000 teachers in Portugal.

DG CONNECT at the summit 10 to 12 November; EVP Henna Virkkunen in a fireside chat on Europe's tech sovereignty, Centre Stage, 10 November 11:05; EU masterclasses on data spaces for SMEs, building AI in Europe, HaDEA funding and free EuroHPC access; stands E415, E418, E405 in Pavilion 4.

story_candidates.title: Web Summit Lisbon: your first day, from airport to arena
story_candidates.angle: A practical, friendly guide for participants: where to collect a wristband from Saturday, the metro stop 300 metres away, what to bring, the app that holds your ticket, and the first-timers' meetup on Tuesday. Brief 2's first principle: value for the participant.
story_candidates.note: The registration capture says times may change: keep that line in the story.

story_candidates.title: Europe arrives in Pavilion 4: the Commission's week at Web Summit
story_candidates.angle: Europe shows up to help builders: a fireside chat on tech sovereignty on Centre Stage, masterclasses on AI, data spaces and free supercomputer access, EU funding sessions, and three stands side by side; and a Dutch delegation with its own lounge. Dinis's 'massive push' on Europe.

story_candidates.title: Road 2 Web Summit: Portugal's startups head for Lisbon
story_candidates.angle: Eleven editions of a programme that brings up to 125 Portuguese startups to the summit, with a bootcamp, a place on the Portugal stand and prizes; last year's cohort of 115 raised 40 million euros.
story_candidates.note: Not known from the captures: this year's selected startups and the size of the Portugal stand (see gaps).

story_candidates.title: From the PITCH stage to new markets: Portuguese startups raising
story_candidates.angle: Two past PITCH winners, Granter and Intuitivo, and Porto's Seamoretech have each closed rounds to grow abroad (Spain, Germany, Italy, Brazil): Portuguese startups taking their ideas to new markets.
story_candidates.note: Seamoretech has no Web Summit link in its capture: either say so or keep it to the two PITCH winners.

story_candidates.title: Web Summit 2026 in numbers: 70,000 people, 10,000 startups
story_candidates.angle: The scale of the week, from Web Summit's own figures: 70,000+ attendees from 100+ countries, 10,000 startups, 17 tracks; and what its first State of the Industry survey found about AI at work (55% say it sharpens their thinking).
story_candidates.note: Report the survey fairly: 60% also say AI increased their workload. The 2025 startup numbers are last year's; say so.

story_candidates.title: Gender in Tech report: 84% see women in leadership
story_candidates.angle: Web Summit's seventh Gender in Tech report: most respondents now see women in leadership, a third at C-suite level. Lead with that progress, and report the rest (half still face sexism, 42% have considered leaving) as the report does, so the story is positive and fair.
story_candidates.note: The 84% is of respondents reporting women in leadership at their company, not of companies; the title keeps that wording.

story_candidates.title: The Portugal banner: awards, funding and the Algarve's plan
story_candidates.angle: Short items for the Portugal banner (brief 6): Unicorn Factory Lisboa's 2026 awards (BloodFlow, knok, RTBeamTech), Algarve Evolution's plan to help create 150 startups by 2032, and the funding rounds in S4.
